section: Red Hat OpenShift Pipelines Operator in a restricted environment

section: Uninstalling OpenShift Pipelines
job_statement: When I need to fully remove OpenShift Pipelines from my cluster, I want to cleanly uninstall all components and custom resources, so I can ensure no residual configuration or resources remain that could interfere with future installations or cluster operations.
prerequisites: Understand that uninstallation will delete all pipelines and tasks
related_jobs: Back up existing pipelines before uninstallation
desired_outcomes: Minimize time required to completely remove all Pipelines components
Ensure no orphaned resources remain after uninstallation
Reduce likelihood of conflicts during future reinstallation
Prevent accidental deletion of important pipeline resources
evidence: install_config-combined.adoc, lines 335-393: Assembly abstract states 'Cluster administrators can uninstall the Pipelines Operator by performing the following steps: Delete the Custom Resources (CRs) for the optional components, TektonHub and TektonResult, if these CRs exist, and then delete the TektonConfig CR. Uninstall the Pipelines Operator. Delete the Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) of the operator.tekton.dev group.'
notes: Main decommissioning job for the entire Pipelines lifecycle. Requires careful sequencing to avoid orphaned components. Documentation emphasizes the importance of CR deletion before operator removal.

section: Deleting the OpenShift Pipelines custom resources
job_statement: As a Cluster administrator, when I need to prepare for Pipelines Operator uninstallation, I want to delete custom resources in the correct order (TektonHub, TektonResult, then TektonConfig), so I can avoid orphaning optional components that cannot be removed later.
parent_job: When I need to fully remove OpenShift Pipelines from my cluster, I want to cleanly uninstall all components and custom resources, so I can ensure no residual configuration or resources remain that could interfere with future installations or cluster operations.
prerequisites: Have cluster administrator access to web console
Understand which optional components are installed
related_jobs: Verify no critical pipelines are running
Export pipeline definitions if needed for backup
desired_outcomes: Ensure optional components are fully removed before operator deletion
Minimize risk of leaving orphaned TektonHub or TektonResult instances
Complete CR deletion with correct sequencing in minimal time
evidence: install_config-combined.adoc, lines 361-392: Procedure states 'You can remove the Pipelines custom resources (CRs) to clean up the configuration before uninstalling the Operator. This involves deleting optional components such as TektonHub and TektonResult, followed by the main TektonConfig CR.' Lines 384-392 include CAUTION: 'Deleting the CRs also deletes the Pipelines components and all the tasks and pipelines on the cluster.' and IMPORTANT: 'If you uninstall the Operator without removing the TektonHub and TektonResult CRs, you cannot remove the Tekton Hub and Tekton Results components later.'
notes: Web console approach for CR deletion. Critical sequencing requirement. Documentation provides strong warnings about consequences of skipping this step.

section: Uninstalling the Red Hat OpenShift Pipelines Operator
job_statement: As a Cluster administrator, when I have deleted all custom resources, I want to uninstall the Pipelines Operator through the web console, so I can remove the operator subscription and all operand instances from my cluster.
parent_job: When I need to fully remove OpenShift Pipelines from my cluster, I want to cleanly uninstall all components and custom resources, so I can ensure no residual configuration or resources remain that could interfere with future installations or cluster operations.
prerequisites: Delete all custom resources (TektonHub, TektonResult, TektonConfig)
related_jobs: Back up secrets from openshift-pipelines namespace if needed
desired_outcomes: Remove operator and all operand instances in single operation
Ensure all resources in openshift-pipelines namespace are deleted
Minimize manual cleanup steps after operator removal
evidence: install_config-combined.adoc, lines 402-421: Procedure states 'You can uninstall the Pipelines Operator by using the OCP web console to remove the Pipelines service from your cluster. This process involves deleting the Operator subscription and its associated operand instances.' Lines 416-421 include WARNING: 'When you uninstall the Pipelines Operator, the uninstallation process deletes all resources within the openshift-pipelines target namespace where Pipelines is installed, including the secrets you configured.'
notes: Web console approach using OperatorHub. Requires prior CR deletion. Warning about namespace-wide deletion including secrets highlights need for backup planning.

section: Deleting the custom resource definitions of the operator.tekton.dev group
job_statement: As a Cluster administrator, when I have uninstalled the Pipelines Operator, I want to delete all operator.tekton.dev CRDs, so I can ensure complete removal of all Pipelines traces and prevent conflicts with future installations.
parent_job: When I need to fully remove OpenShift Pipelines from my cluster, I want to cleanly uninstall all components and custom resources, so I can ensure no residual configuration or resources remain that could interfere with future installations or cluster operations.
related_jobs: Verify no other operators depend on these CRDs
desired_outcomes: Remove all residual CRD definitions created during installation
Ensure clean slate for potential future Pipelines installation
Minimize time to identify and delete all operator.tekton.dev CRDs
evidence: install_config-combined.adoc, lines 431-449: Procedure states 'You can delete the operator.tekton.dev custom resource definitions (CRDs) to fully remove all Pipelines traces from your cluster. This step ensures that no residual definitions remain after the Operator uninstallation.' Line 437: 'Delete the CustomResourceDefinitions of the operator.tekton.dev group. The Pipelines Operator creates these CRDs by default during installation.'
notes: Final cleanup step. Web console approach using CRD filtering. CRDs are created automatically during installation and must be manually deleted during complete removal.

section: Automatic pruning of task runs and pipeline runs
job_statement: When managing cluster resources over time, I want to automatically remove completed TaskRun and PipelineRun objects, so I can prevent resource exhaustion and maintain optimal cluster performance.
desired_outcomes: Minimize cluster resource consumption from stale objects

evidence: install_config-combined.adoc -> Automatic pruning of task runs and pipeline runs (lines 1426-1436): 'You can automatically prune stale TaskRun and PipelineRun resources to free up cluster resources. Pipelines provides a configurable pruner that removes unused objects based on your policies.'
notes: Core operational job for lifecycle management. Two implementation approaches: scheduled (cron-based) and event-driven (real-time).

section: Configuring the pruner
job_statement: When I need scheduled cleanup of pipeline resources, I want to configure time-based or count-based retention policies in TektonConfig, so I can maintain a predictable number of recent runs while automatically removing older resources.
parent_job: Automatically remove completed TaskRun and PipelineRun objects

evidence: install_config-combined.adoc -> Configuring the pruner (lines 1446-1506): Example shows schedule (cron), keep (count), keep-since (time-based), and prune-per-resource settings. 'The default schedule runs the process at 08:00 every day.' 'If you set keep to 100, then the pruner keeps 100 most recent task runs and 100 most recent pipeline runs.'
notes: User story for scheduled/cron-based pruning approach. Alternative to event-driven approach.

section: Annotations for automatically pruning task runs and pipeline runs

These annotations allow you to override global pruning settings.' Lists operator.tekton.dev/prune.* annotations and example with keep-since: 7200.
notes: Namespace-level override pattern for scheduled pruner.

section: Enabling the event-driven pruner
job_statement: When I need near real-time cleanup instead of scheduled batches, I want to enable the event-based pruner controller, so I can delete completed runs immediately after they finish without waiting for cron schedules.
parent_job: Automatically remove completed TaskRun and PipelineRun objects
related_jobs: Configure TTL or history limits for event pruner
desired_outcomes: Minimize delay between completion and cleanup
Reduce cluster resource spikes from batch pruning

evidence: install_config-combined.adoc -> Enabling the event-driven pruner (lines 1563-1643): 'You can enable the event-based pruner to delete completed PipelineRun and TaskRun resources in near real-time.' 'You must disable the job-based pruner in the TektonConfig CR before you enable the event-driven pruner.' Example shows spec.pruner.disabled: true and spec.tektonpruner.disabled: false.
notes: User story for event-driven pruning approach. Mutually exclusive with scheduled pruner. More immediate cleanup.
